study: Drummond et al. 2011, Thinking Reader (NCEE 2010-4035, REL-NEI)
eval_evidence: AIR/REL Northeast & Islands led the evaluation; the developer (CAST) and distributor (Tom Snyder Productions) were deliberately kept out of evaluation roles 'to minimize a potential source of bias' (front matter; design ch.).
developer_evidence: CAST, 'the developer of Thinking Reader, oversaw implementation and conducted teacher training along with staff from Tom Snyder Productions, the software distributor' (PD chapter).
cascade_evidence: Developer (CAST) staff and the distributor's trainers trained the grade-6 teachers directly; two 6-hr group sessions + three individual coaching visits, no train-the-trainer layer.
counterfactual_evidence: Control = business-as-usual regular grade-6 ELA instruction; intervention used as a partial substitute for regular ELA (design/notes).
coaching_evidence: PD = two 6-hr group sessions plus three individual coaching visits over 2008-09 (~7.5-8.5 hrs total); a few periodic coaching visits, not recurring monthly in-class cycles.
student_dose_evidence: Thinking Reader is a digital reading-comprehension software (3 digital novels) with animated coaches that 'act as instructors'; students worked in the software as a partial substitute for regular ELA -> substantial student-facing software dose.
maturity_evidence: Outcomes measured spring 2009 at the end of the single 2008-09 implementation year; teachers newly trained that summer/fall (single immediate post wave).
